scope: Method/data-contract review and public aggregate metadata only; zero real row parsing, candidate fitting or new performance evidence.
source_capture: Primary papers were opened for technical review; URLs, version and notes are saved here, not full paper copies or external benchmark scores.

primary_sources.title: Evaluation of Session-based Recommendation Algorithms
primary_sources.supports: Standard adjacent-transition MC and session-kNN definitions; D1 below is our own controlled variant, not their MC implementation.

primary_sources.title: Collaborative Filtering for Implicit Feedback Datasets
primary_sources.supports: Confidence-weighted implicit-feedback factorization with alternating least squares.

primary_sources.title: BPR: Bayesian Personalized Ranking from Implicit Feedback
primary_sources.supports: Pairwise ranking criterion and sampling-based learning; the criterion still needs a chosen underlying model.

primary_sources.title: Embarrassingly Shallow Autoencoders for Sparse Data
primary_sources.supports: Regularized item-item Gram inverse and zero-diagonal linear weights; standard dense formulation has quadratic item storage.

candidates.data_fit: Existing ordered view baskets, session IDs and C1 support suffice without item features or persistent user factors.
candidates.reason: Deterministic exact sparse counts; preserves C1 session unit, denominator, history and tie/fill rules. Changes only the joint directional-adjacency relation; no training hyperparameters or search.
candidates.limitation: Not standard first-order MC, not a probability, not a solution to unsupported items.

candidates.data_fit: Train session item sets and current session history are available; unknown visitor ID alone is not a blocker.
candidates.reason: Would require fixed similarity, neighbor count, exact neighbor search or an explicit sampling policy, tie rules and separate cost/oracle work.
candidates.limitation: Pure interaction neighbors do not learn associations for train-unsupported items; runtime not measured here.

candidates.data_fit: A train visitor/session-item matrix can be defined, but that representation and causal new-session fold-in are not yet contracted.
candidates.reason: Requires latent dimension, confidence mapping, regularization, iteration, initialization/seeds and new-user rules.
candidates.limitation: Does not automatically solve new-user or unsupported-item gaps; no fit or library installation in this round.

candidates.data_fit: Implicit train interactions exist; must separately choose underlying model and sampling universe.
candidates.reason: Adds pairwise sampling, optimization, initialization, fixed seeds and convergence decisions.
candidates.limitation: Unobserved items are not proven dislikes; no negative-sampling or stochastic-model scope is introduced this round.

candidates.data_fit: Binary implicit session-item data are compatible in principle.
candidates.reason: One dense float64 item-item matrix already exceeds the planned 8 GiB process budget; sparse/low-rank approximations would be different methods.
candidates.limitation: Storage calculation is a structural estimate, not a measured runtime or peak-memory benchmark.

dense_EASE_structural_estimate.excluded: Additional matrices, factorization workspace and runtime

selection.selection_basis: Contract alignment, controlled representation change, exact auditability and feasible sparse design; not measured D1 superiority.
